title: On Tackling the leak before breakfast
subtitle: 困难与应对 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 困难与应对（做人与做事·困难与应对）
meta: 主题语境：困难与应对（做人与做事·困难与应对）　|　核心词汇：tackle　|　正文 345 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 tackle 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1986 the director ① tackled the leak before breakfast year after year, and every actor in the theatre said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three nights on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the director ② tackles the leak before breakfast for the whole place without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ tackle the leak before breakfast at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ tackled the leak before breakfast before — a line in the poster for August 1980 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Tackling the leak before breakfast year after year, the director said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the script at the far stage, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ tackle the biggest boy in the yard for the whole place, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Tackle the biggest boy in the yard at once and never mention it again.

By 1993 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the poster, and a new actor from the next theatre ⑧ tackles the biggest boy in the yard year after year every night without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the stage, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ tackled the leak before breakfast again when nobody else would.

⑩ To tackle the leak before breakfast, my mother said in 1998, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the theatre remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the theatre forgets, somebody tackles the leak before breakfast for the whole place again and somebody must tackle the leak before breakfast year after year all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 着手处理（一般过去式 tackled the leak before breakfast：1986 年导演头一回这样做，年年地）
B. v. 着手处理（一般现在 tackles the leak before breakfast：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 着手处理（不定式 to tackle the leak before breakfast：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 着手处理（过去完成时 had tackled the leak before breakfast：1980 年八月的戏报上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 着手处理（动名词 tackling the leak before breakfast 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 擒抱（tackle the biggest boy in the yard：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去擒抱在院子里把最大的男孩抱摔倒）
G. v. 擒抱（tackle the biggest boy in the yard：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 着手处理（后段两处：新来的演员照例 tackles the biggest boy in the yard，而母亲又一次 tackled the leak before breakfast）

items.q: to tackle the leak before breakfast
tackled the leak before breakfast before
tackle the biggest boy in the yard for the whole place
tackle the biggest boy in the yard at once
tackles the biggest boy in the yard year after year
tackled the leak before breakfast again
to tackle the leak before breakfast

answers.why: tackle 意为“着手处理”，1986 年导演年年地着手处理早饭前就动手堵那个漏处，那是戏院里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 tackled。
tackle 意为“着手处理”，自那以后导演替所有人把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 tackles。
tackle 意为“着手处理”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯着手处理早饭前就动手堵那个漏处”，此处为不定式 to tackle the leak before breakfast。
tackle 意为“着手处理”，戏报里 八月 那行字说明早在 1993 年之前就有人着手处理过，故用过去完成时 had tackled。
tackle 意为“着手处理”，导演说“着手处理早饭前就动手堵那个漏处这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 tackling the leak before breakfast 作主语。
tackle 意为“擒抱”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去擒抱在院子里把最大的男孩抱摔倒”，should ever 之后用原形 tackle the biggest boy in the yard。
tackle 意为“擒抱”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻擒抱在院子里把最大的男孩抱摔倒（tackle the biggest boy in the yard at once），以后再也不要提起。
tackle 意为“着手处理”，新来的演员每个夜晚都照例擒抱在院子里把最大的男孩抱摔倒，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 tackles。
tackle 意为“着手处理”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次年年地着手处理早饭前就动手堵那个漏处，用一般过去式 tackled 叙述。
tackle 意为“着手处理”，结尾那句是母亲 1998 年的话：要着手处理早饭前就动手堵那个漏处，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和戏院记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 tackle 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1986 the director tackled the leak before breakfast year after year, and nobody in the theatre forgot it.
Even now the director tackles the leak before breakfast for the whole place whenever the theatre asks.
Tackling the leak before breakfast year after year, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever tackle the biggest boy in the yard for the whole place, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new actor from the next theatre tackles the biggest boy in the yard year after year every night, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother tackled the leak before breakfast again, and the theatre remembered that half.
